constants.description: Near-point distance used to define magnifying power
constants.source_title: University Physics Volume 3, Section 2.7 The Simple Magnifier
constants.locator: Equation 2.32, M = 25 cm / f for an image at infinity, and the sentence after it
constants.quote: The resulting magnification is simply the ratio of the near-point distance to the focal length of the magnifying lens.

assumptions: The lens is taken to be a single lens with two equally curved faces, made of material with a refractive index of 1.5. For such a lens the focal length equals the radius of curvature (lens maker's equation, OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, Section 2.4, Equation 2.21: 1/f = (n − 1)(1/R1 − 1/R2)). The index is an assumption with no cited source.
A lens cannot be wider than the sphere its curved surface is part of, so its diameter cannot exceed twice the radius of curvature.
Magnifying power is taken as 250 mm ÷ focal length, the convention for an image at infinity.

A diameter up to 2× the limit is reported as a flag, not a hard result, to allow for denser glass and for the other convention for magnifying power. This margin is a team choice, not a physical constant.
The listing does not describe a Fresnel or flat sheet lens, so an ordinary curved lens is assumed.
